sessions.note: Ran the ra_solver pipeline on the banked score-22 candidate. Extraction + simulate validate 3/3 against the dump (free regression check on the solver itself). The function has only THREE global allocnos: 75 = t (nrefs 8, livelen 17, -> $a1), 72 = var_s0 (-> $s0), 74 = ff (-> $s1); everything else is local-alloc. hard_conflicts[75] = {2,3,4}, i.e. $v0, $v1 and $a0 are all blocked for t, which is why it lands in $a1 while target wants $v1. perturb.py with spec {75:3}, singles + pairs + greedy: NO sufficient vector in the searched space. That is the structurally correct answer rather than a search failure - the $v1 block on t is pseudo 83, the sign-extended var_s0, which is a LOCAL-alloc quantity, and ra_solver simulates global.c only. Local-alloc runs first and is outside the modeled space, so no global-allocno atom can move t. To reach target, local-alloc must place the sign-extend somewhere other than $v1; it scans ascending, so that needs $v0, $v1 and $a0 all occupied across the sign-extend's live range. $v0 (offset arithmetic) and $a0 (the call argument) are occupied; $v1 is not. In target $v1 holds the 24 - so target's 24 constant is a LOCAL quantity allocated before the sign-extend, while ours is a global allocno. RTL check via tmp/ra/rtl.py: all four references to pseudo 75 sit inside the loop-body block, so the promotion to global is a local-alloc decision, not a cross-block one. NEW MEASURED NEGATIVES this round: t declared at loop-body block scope and the named sign-extend local both produce a register mapping BIT-IDENTICAL to the candidate; the shift-expression-first form changes the shape for the worse (42 differing lines vs 40) without fixing the swap; routing the 1 through the offset variable after the stores gives 74 insns; and t = (s16)var_s0 with buf[0] = 1 << t also gives 74 insns. GENERAL FINDING for the solver: when a residual is decided by local-alloc, ra_solver is structurally blind to it - worth recording as a scope limit of the tool. src/main.c reverted; working tree clean.

sessions.note: Phase 5 of the ra_solver extends the model past global.c to local-alloc.c, and this function is the first payoff because Phase 4 had shown its residual is decided entirely by local-alloc. The new tools (tools/ra_solver/local_extract.py + local_alloc.py) reproduce this function EXACTLY: 2/2 blocks on the qty ordering and 10/10 quantities on the assignment. Block 2, the loop body, in allocation order: qty 2 (refs 18, span [48,60), pri 60000) -> $v0; qty 1 (refs 30, span [10,34), pri 50000) -> $v0; qty 0 (refs 18, span [6,38), pri 22500) -> $v1, this is the sign-extended var_s0; qty 3 (refs 4, span [54,58), pri 20000) -> $v1. find_free_reg scans ascending, so the sign-extend takes $v1 because only $v0 is occupied across its range. Target holds it in $a1, which requires $v0, $v1 AND $a0 all occupied there. Replaying the block (tmp/ra/tmv_local.py) gives a TWO-PART requirement and neither part alone suffices: one extra quantity overlapping [6,38) with priority above 22500 (for instance refs 8 and span 10 or less) moves the sign-extend only as far as $a0; hard $a0 live across [6,38) on its own leaves it in $v1; BOTH together put it in $a1, which is target. This finally explains why the call-argument naming family (s32 *p = buf and its variants, the hoist-call-arg-local-flips-jal-delay LUID lever) was uniformly inert at 22: it only ever addressed part 2. Target supplies part 2 by emitting addiu a0,sp,16 EARLY, before the address arithmetic, so hard $a0 is live across the sign-extend's range, whereas we emit it late. For a future attempt: both parts must land at once, and part 1 needs a short-lived high-reference LOCAL quantity inside the loop body. Note that t has 8 references but is currently a GLOBAL allocno spanning the whole loop body, so it does not qualify as-is; making it short-lived and block-local would satisfy part 1, but the reason it is multi-set in the first place is to defeat loop.c's move_movables hoist, so the two requirements pull against each other. src/main.c reverted.
